message:
I run deliveries for a small furniture restorer and I've got a few things to sort for tomorrow.

Can you suggest a name for our new delivery van (staff vote, nothing rude)?

Tomorrow the van can't leave the depot before 08:30 and must be back by 12:00. Three drops, each takes 15 minutes to unload. Drop A has a delivery window of 09:00 to 10:00. Drop B is a shop that needs its delivery done before it opens at 09:30. Drop C is an office that won't accept anything before 11:00. Driving times: depot to A 30 min, depot to B 20 min, depot to C 45 min, A to B 25 min, A to C 40 min, B to C 50 min. The driver also needs a 30-minute break somewhere before 12:00. What order should he go in, and what's the timeline?

Could you also rewrite our delivery text so it sounds friendlier than "Driver arriving. Be in."? List three things the driver should check on furniture before handing it over. Should we give customers a paper delivery note or an emailed one? And define "proof of delivery" in a line for our new part-timer. One more thing: we're thinking of texting customers the evening before with a rough arrival time. Could you draft that evening-before text too, keeping it under 160 characters so it goes as a single message?
response:
Here's everything, starting with tomorrow's route.

## Route: Depot → B → A → C → Depot

**B → A → C is the only order that works:**

- **A can't go first.** The van would reach A at 09:00 at the earliest, finish unloading at 09:15, and get to B at 09:40, after B's 09:30 opening.
- **C must go last.** It won't accept anything before 11:00, and A's window ends at 10:00.

**Timeline:**

| Time | Activity |
|---|---|
| **08:30** | Leave depot |
| **08:50** | Arrive B (20 min drive) |
| 08:50–09:05 | Unload at B ✅ done well before 09:30 opening |
| 09:05–09:30 | Drive B → A (25 min) |
| **09:30–09:45** | Unload at A ✅ within the 09:00–10:00 window |
| 09:45–10:25 | Drive A → C (40 min) |
| **10:25–10:55** | **30-minute break**, near C while waiting for it to accept deliveries |
| **11:00–11:15** | Unload at C ✅ not before 11:00 |
| 11:15–12:00 | Drive C → depot (45 min) |
| **12:00** | Back at depot ✅ just in time |

**Warning: there's no slack at the end.** The van gets back at exactly 12:00, so any delay at C or in traffic on the way back means a late return. The early part of the day has spare time but the end doesn't. The plan also assumes the C → depot drive takes 45 minutes, the same as depot → C.

To build in some margin:

- **Ask C whether they could accept at 10:30 or 10:45.** The van arrives at 10:25, so even a slightly earlier time helps.
- **Check whether the 12:00 return is firm,** or whether a few minutes' leeway would be acceptable.
- **Make sure the driver stays close to C** during the break so he can unload as soon as it's 11:00.

## Van name ideas

- **Sir Haul-a-Lot**
- **The Wardrobe Wagon**
- **Chester Drawers**
- **Van Gogh** (fitting for a restorer)
- **The Varnish Van**
- **Dovetail Dave**

"Chester Drawers" or "Van Gogh" would probably go down well in a staff vote.

## Friendlier "on the way" text

> Hi [Name], it's [Driver] from [Company]. I'm on my way with your furniture and should be with you in about [20] minutes. See you soon!

If you need to make sure someone is in, you could add: *"If you're not going to be home, just reply and we'll sort out another time."*

## Three things to check before handing over furniture

1. **Condition:** no new scratches, dents, chips or scuffs from the journey. Compare with photos taken at loading if you have them. Ask the customer to look it over with the driver.
2. **Completeness and function:** all parts, shelves, keys, handles and fixings are present, and doors, drawers and hinges open and close smoothly.
3. **Placement and stability:** it's in the spot the customer wants, sitting level and steady, with any wall fixings attached if that's part of the service.

## Paper or emailed delivery note?

**Emailed, with the customer signing on the driver's phone or tablet.** It's quicker, doesn't get lost, and gives you a record with time and signature. Carry **a few paper notes as a backup** for customers who prefer paper or when the device fails.

As a restorer, you might also leave a printed **care card** with the furniture, covering how to clean it, which polish to use and what to avoid. It's a thoughtful touch, and customers often keep it.

## "Proof of delivery" for the new part-timer

> **Proof of delivery is the record, usually the customer's signature plus the date, time and a photo, that shows we delivered the item to the right person in good condition.**

## Evening-before text (under 160 characters)

> Hi [Name], your furniture from [Company] arrives tomorrow, [9-11am]. We'll text when the driver sets off. Questions? Call [number].

With a typical name, company name and phone number filled in, it comes to about **140–145 characters**. For example, "Sarah," "Hartwell Restoration," "9-11am" and "01234 567890" give **143 characters**. If your company name is long, check the final length.

Two tips to keep it to a single text message:

- **Avoid emojis and "smart" curly quotes or apostrophes.** Either can switch the message to a format that allows only 70 characters per part, which splits it into several texts.
- **Use timeline-based windows for tomorrow:** B about 08:30–09:00, A about 09:15–09:45, and C at 11:00. A window of roughly 30 minutes is reassuring for customers without boxing the driver in.
